findings.description: ttlDays=0 is permitted by validation but results in expires_at equal to creation time. The list() filter uses strict greater-than (Date.parse(expires_at) > now), so notifications created with ttlDays=0 become immediately unlistable and effectively invisible. Consider requiring ttlDays >= 1 or using >= in the expiry comparison.

markRead unconditionally sets read=true regardless of any input payload. While the acceptance criteria only requires {read: true} to mark as read, the service signature does not accept a read parameter, so a hypothetical {read: false} cannot be handled at this layer. This is acceptable for Phase 1 but worth noting if the API contract evolves.

body.length counts UTF-16 code units rather than Unicode code points/grapheme clusters. Strings containing surrogate pairs (e.g., emoji) may be rejected slightly earlier than a strict 500-character interpretation. Conservative and safe, but may differ from a UI-side character counter.

purgeExpired() is provided but never invoked automatically; expired notifications remain in memory until explicitly purged. The list() path filters them out, so behavior is correct, but memory could grow unbounded without scheduled purging. Not a defect given the in-memory Phase 1 scope.

independent_verifier.summary: The NotificationService correctly satisfies all AH-CAPMAP-020 acceptance criteria: create() produces notifications with id, user_id, type, title, body, created_at, read=false (plus expires_at/seq); list() returns unread items sorted by created_at desc with include_read support; markRead() and dismiss() enforce ownership; the five required types are validated; 30-day TTL is configurable; no external delivery is present; and body is capped at 500 chars. Error handling is robust (empty user/title, invalid type, oversized body, invalid clock, duplicate/empty id, ownership checks). Immutability is preserved via Object.freeze and defensive copies. Findings are minor edge cases and operational notes, none of which violate the requirements.
